correctness.rationale: The exact identity for a cross-class swap follows by cancelling both agents' mutual distance in before/after costs; a positive sum of two strictly positive improvements increases the finite-state potential. The potential and total welfare are each represented as nonnegative gap-weighted sums of concave quadratics in prefix rank counts. The respective nearest-integer prescriptions attain each gap optimum simultaneously because their clamped prefix counts increase by zero or one, from zero to a. The \(K_{2,5}\) counterexample enumerates all seven indistinguishable type-pair classes, certifying cross-cost minimum 15 and stable minimum 17. Star bounds are direct median and triangle inequalities. A standalone exact-integer program corroborates 2,674 families, 64,548 partitions, 803,860 swaps, both optimal algorithms and sharpness. Finite tests are not asserted to prove arbitrary real inputs.

value.rationale: The complete bipartite graph is the basic nonregular extension of the all-regular Schelling convergence theorem; the exact two-agent gain identity explains why it remains convergent. Sorting yields efficient, fully constructive equilibria and globally optimal social assignments even with highly unequal community sizes. The exact 17/15 loss on \(K_{2,5}\) establishes a motivated efficiency boundary absent from the regular case, and the sharp \(n-1\) star price of anarchy quantifies extreme stable inefficiency. These are robust all-size properties, not routine restatements of an enumerated instance.
